20. Command reference

Generated by u2ue/manual/build.py from the facade's verb registry (u2ue/verbs/__init__.py) and each verb's own docstring - edit the code, not this page.

Who this is for: the toolkit developer and the reviewer - each verb's full usage text, exactly as the code prints it; read it when Chapter 19 or a procedure names a verb's option.

Every command runs from the toolkit's root (the folder that holds u2ue/):

py -m u2ue                                   # list every verb
py -m u2ue find <words>                      # search everything the toolkit holds (no project)
py -m u2ue --project <name|file.json> <verb> [options]
verb needs a project what it does
find no search everything the toolkit holds: verbs, adapters, tools, docs, measured rules, converter stages, routes
estimate no what porting a Unity project will cost in model tokens: its code and assets read, times rates measured on a real port, with the cache split, the list cost and the confidence
port yes the whole port as one command: every stage in order, each read from its own records; runs what a verb can, stops with one question where a person, the AI or an editor is needed
info yes every path the project names, OPENED; its adapter
inventory yes the game's own C#, type by type: Unity API by family, pure rules, the frame order (no editor runs)
uml yes the game's class model off its own code roots (and its model once scaffolded): extract, mermaid, where, ask
scaffold yes the engine-free model a game's rules move into: created, declared in the project file, built and gated
logic yes where this project's logic port stands: each u2ue-logic skill step judged by its own DONE WHEN, read from its records
data yes a component's or ScriptableObject's serialized values off a scene / prefab / asset, overrides applied (no editor runs)
shear yes the scene nodes Unreal cannot place as Unity does (a sheared transform chain), with the error in cm
scene yes a Unity scene as an Unreal level: export (in a window), import, readback, and the fidelity gate against its own baseline
parity yes the game's rules on every runtime they run on, compared by float bits with a characterised allowance
digest yes the game's rule cases answered with no engine: on CoreCLR (Headless) and on that Unity's own Mono (UnityMono)
host yes the game's OWN Unreal project, made as a customer makes one: create, install, compile, generate, wire, publish, run
ui yes a Unity UI screen converted to a folder Unreal reads; the generic uGUI / TextMeshPro library's tests
window yes ONE Unity measurement window from a data file: idle-gated, owner-stoppable, nothing replaced, md5-held
trial yes a route's TRIAL in Unreal from a data file: build, resave, read, judge, photos; one Unreal at a time, stoppable
conform yes data-first conformance over all keys: Unity's particle state (one generic probe) against Niagara's readback, paired by file id
judge yes every judge the trials run, the trials that run it, and whether its plant can refuse (its --selftest, or a trial's declared plant)
extract yes Unity prefabs -> the engine-neutral IR (no editor runs)
check yes the toolkit's selftests, the project's field gates, the measured rules' Unity versions
build yes IR -> Niagara systems under the project's content root (Unreal, headless)
read yes the built systems read back frame by frame (Unreal, headless)
photo yes the built systems photographed, paired with Unity's frames (Unreal, headless)
report yes the acceptance page from the project's records
metrics yes the port's numbers, each from a record, with its definition
tempo yes each verified route's first code -> verified flip, read off git
cycle yes every pillar of the product checked: PASS / FAIL / HELD by a named decision / ABSENT (no check yet)
tool yes one tool of the toolkit run by hand, found by its file name, with the project's variables (u2ue/env.py)
release no the package as a repo: assembled from the toolkit's own trees by one manifest, secrets refused, public readiness counted

find

search everything the toolkit holds: verbs, adapters, tools, docs, measured rules, converter stages, routes.

u2ue find - search everything the toolkit holds (u2ue/catalog.py): verbs, adapters, tools, doc sections, measured Unity rules,
converter functions and stages, verified routes. No project needed.

    py -m u2ue find <words ...> [--kind concept,verb,adapter,tool,doc,rule,converter,route] [--top N] [--selftest]

Every word must appear (in the name, the summary or the body); the results come grouped by kind, best first, each with WHERE it
lives (file:line) - the place to open next.

estimate

what porting a Unity project will cost in model tokens: its code and assets read, times rates measured on a real port, with the cache split, the list cost and the confidence.

u2ue estimate - what porting a Unity project will cost in model tokens on Opus 5.5, from MEASURED rates (u2ue/estimate.py).

    py -m u2ue estimate --unity <Unity project> [--roots A,B] [--model M] [--json OUT]    point it at any Unity project
    py -m u2ue --project <name> estimate [--json OUT]                                       the project's unity.root and code.roots
    py -m u2ue.verbs.estimate --selftest

What it prints, every number with where it came from:
  the project   READ off its files (Census): the C# code lines per top folder, split COUPLED (uses a Unity API family, a lifecycle
                method or a Unity base) and PURE; Editor folders apart (not ported); scenes in the build settings; particle
                prefabs; prefabs and scenes with a Canvas. With no --roots every folder under Assets is counted and listed, so the
                game's own folders can be named (vendor packages live in Assets too) - the logic line is then an upper bound
  the estimate  per stage: the logic (AI - lines x the measured tokens per line of the reference port's extraction, all-in),
                the conductor's stops (AI - one turn each at the measured tokens per call), everything a verb does (AUTOMATIC -
                no model tokens); the total in the five token kinds, the share the prompt cache served, the list cost at the
                model's READ prices (u2ue/basis/prices.json), the same calls' cost with no caching, a bootstrap band
  the saving    what the reference port's agents spent per unit on the stages the verbs now do (scenes), where measured
  confidence    HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW per stage and why (samples, the model it was measured on, how far outside the basis)

The basis (u2ue/basis/tokens.json) is written by u2ue/survey/token_basis.py from a project's own records. Exit 0 = estimated;
2 = refused (no Unity project, no price for the model, a basis with a rate missing).

port

the whole port as one command: every stage in order, each read from its own records; runs what a verb can, stops with one question where a person, the AI or an editor is needed.

u2ue port - the whole port as ONE command (u2ue/port.py: PortPlan, Stage, PortRun).

    py -m u2ue --project <name> port                       every stage's state, read from its records, and the next action
    py -m u2ue --project <name> port --run                 also run the AUTOMATIC stages that are TODO, in order
    py -m u2ue --project <name> port --run --with-unreal   ... the ones that launch a headless Unreal too (one at a time)
    py -m u2ue.verbs.port --selftest

Without --run nothing is started but the read-only checks (info, host status, scene check, check --only gates, parity). With
--run each AUTOMATIC stage that reads TODO runs through its own verb and is read again; a RED stage holds back only the stages that wait on it. An
EDITOR stage never runs here (a Unity editor is the owner's: its window is named, and `u2ue window` runs one only while the editor
is idle); an AI stage hands over to the skill (u2ue-logic, kept going by u2ue-long-run); an OWNER stage asks its question.
Running it again resumes: every state is read from the records each time.

Exit 0 = nothing left (every stage DONE, or ABSENT / UNCHECKED and said); 1 = something is left, the next action printed;
2 = refused. --run writes <work.records>/port/port-<stamp>.json and port-latest.json.

info

every path the project names, OPENED; its adapter.

u2ue info - every path the project names, OPENED (exit 1 when an INPUT is missing), its adapter and its key source.

inventory

the game's own C#, type by type: Unity API by family, pure rules, the frame order (no editor runs).

u2ue inventory - what a Unity game's own C# asks of the engine, type by type.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> inventory [--survey] [--roots Assets/A,Assets/B] [--out DIR]

--survey     every top folder under Assets with its count of .cs files (Editor folders apart) - read this first, then name the
             game's own folders as code.roots in the project file (never guessed: vendor packages live in Assets too)
default      reads every .cs under code.roots (the project file's, or --roots) and writes DIR/inventory.json + DIR/inventory.md:
  per type   its kind (MonoBehaviour / ScriptableObject - through the project's own base classes, transitively - or plain, or a base
             the scanned code does not declare, named), its Unity lifecycle methods, and every Unity API it uses by FAMILY, each
             family pointing at the manual's chapter (u2ue/BASICS.md section) that says how it ports
  pure rules the types that use no Unity API at all - what moves into an engine-free model first
  frame      every MonoBehaviour's script execution order (its .cs.meta executionOrder) and the lifecycle methods it has, in
  order      Unity's frame order - the table a frame driver is written from (U2ue.Runtime's UnityFrame takes it)
How it reads: comments and strings are blanked first (a name in a comment or a string is not a use); a brace stack tells which
type a line belongs to (nested types apart); a token counts on word boundaries. It is a LEXICAL reader: a call through an alias,
reflection or a generic helper is not seen - the report says so, and a miss is UNKNOWN, never "does not use".

uml

the game's class model off its own code roots (and its model once scaffolded): extract, mermaid, where, ask.

u2ue uml - the game's class model, off ITS OWN code roots (logic-port skill step 2: "draw the class model of one slice before moving
anything").

    py -m u2ue --project <name> uml extract                           the class model of the game's code (+ its model, once scaffolded)
    py -m u2ue --project <name> uml mermaid --focus TypeA TypeB        a class diagram of a slice, every member a real one
    py -m u2ue --project <name> uml where|ask|callers|tests <Name>     lookups over the same model
    py -m u2ue --project <name> uml <any other uml.py subcommand>

This wraps .opus-tools/uml.py (the facade never rewrites a tool) with the project's roots and its own index folder, so one game's
model never lands on another game's index:
  roots   every code.roots folder under unity.root, then every model.scan folder under model.root once the project declares a model
  index   <work.inventory>/uml (uml.py --cache)
A project with no code.roots is refused: name them first (`u2ue inventory --survey`), never guessed.

scaffold

the engine-free model a game's rules move into: created, declared in the project file, built and gated.

u2ue scaffold - the engine-free model a game's rules move into, created, declared and gated in one command (logic-port skill step 4;
the method's recipe step 1: "Write your Core. An engine-free project with NO references at all").

    py -m u2ue --project <name> scaffold --name <Model> --dir <DIR> [--dry]
    py -m u2ue.verbs.scaffold --selftest

Writes, under DIR (refused if any of it exists - a scaffold never overwrites):
  <Model>.Core/<Model>.Core.csproj              netstandard2.1 (Unity 2021+ loads it) + net8.0 (tests, hosts); it references ONLY
                                                U2ue.Runtime (the toolkit's engine-free frame / clock / coroutine / platform library)
  <Model>.Core/README.md                        what belongs in it, in four lines, and the gate that holds it
  <Model>.Core.Tests/<Model>.Core.Tests.csproj  NUnit, headless (`dotnet test`) - where each ported rule's test goes
and adds the project file's "model" block (root, layers, scan, hosting) - the block `u2ue check --only model` reads - then builds
both projects and runs that check. Exit 0 = the model exists, compiles, and its gates pass on it; 1 = a build or a gate failed;
2 = refused (a model already declared, a path that exists, no --name / --dir).

The bones, in one analogy: the Core is the game's RULEBOOK - it says what happens, never how it looks; the engines are the TABLES
the game is played on. layer_gate keeps any engine out of the rulebook; host_gate keeps platform chores (logging, files, random
numbers) on the one shared shelf, U2ue.Runtime's Platform interfaces, instead of re-declared on every rule's host.

logic

where this project's logic port stands: each u2ue-logic skill step judged by its own DONE WHEN, read from its records.

u2ue logic - where this project's logic port stands: each step of the u2ue-logic skill judged by its own DONE WHEN, read from the
project's records now (u2ue/logic.py: LogicPort). An AI porter, or a person, starts a session here instead of re-deriving the state.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> logic             every step: DONE / NOT YET / JUDGED (a reviewer's call) / NOT RUN (a test run
                                                  it names) - and the step to take next
    py -m u2ue.verbs.logic --selftest             a skill step whose title moved is refused; a project with no model reads NOT YET
                                                  from Step 4; the real skill's steps all have a check
Nothing is written and nothing is built; the checks it runs are the toolkit's own (info, check --only model, parity).

data

a component's or ScriptableObject's serialized values off a scene / prefab / asset, overrides applied (no editor runs).

u2ue data - a component's serialized values, or a ScriptableObject's, READ off the Unity file.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> data --from <Assets/...unity|.prefab|.asset> (--script <ClassName> | --class <id or Unity type>)
                                     [--out FILE.json] [--tsv FILE.tsv] [--no-expand]

What the inspector shows is what the scene or prefab STORES - "Unity serialization beats the C# initializer" - so a port reads it
there and never retypes it. This finds every component that matches:
  --script  a MonoBehaviour whose m_Script is the .cs file named <ClassName>.cs (its guid from the project's guid index - never a
            line number; a file Unity has re-saved moves its lines)
  --class   a built-in component by class id (20 Camera, 4 Transform, 108 Light, ...) or its YAML type name (Camera, Light, ...)
in the file with its NESTED prefab instances expanded and their modifications applied (the IR reader's own u1e_nested: a value an
override changed is the override's), and writes per component: its GameObject's path from the root, its fileID, and every field as
the file stores it - a reference {fileID, guid} carries the asset path it names. --tsv also writes one `<dotted path>   <value>` row
per leaf (lists as path[i]), a form two readers' outputs can be diffed in. A ScriptableObject .asset is one MonoBehaviour: --script
names its class. Bookkeeping fields (m_ObjectHideFlags, m_CorrespondingSourceObject, m_PrefabInstance, m_PrefabAsset,
m_EditorHideFlags, m_EditorClassIdentifier) are left out, every one by that list.

shear

the scene nodes Unreal cannot place as Unity does (a sheared transform chain), with the error in cm.

u2ue shear - the scene nodes Unreal cannot place as Unity does (BASICS section 9).

    py -m u2ue --project <name> shear (--gltf FILE.gltf | --from Assets/....unity|.prefab [--no-expand]) [--json OUT] [--eps 1e-6]

A Unity Transform composes as a MATRIX, so a rotated child under a non-uniformly scaled parent is SHEARED; an Unreal component holds
translation + rotation + scale and drops the shear at every level. For every node this composes its chain BOTH ways (u2ue.transform:
compose_matrix and compose_trs) and reports the sheared ones - the axes' worst |cosine| (nonOrthogonality) and how far the corners
of a unit cube at the node land apart (unitCornerCm) - and whether the node DRAWS (a glTF mesh; in YAML an active MeshRenderer or
SkinnedMeshRenderer on it). A sheared node that draws nothing still moves its children: the list says which. Whether the error is
accepted, baked or fixed in the Unity scene is the porter's call, made WITH the number, and pinned by a gate once made.
--gltf     a scene exported by the scene pipeline (glTFast): its nodes as exported (inactive subtrees left out by the exporter)
--from     the scene or prefab YAML itself, nested prefab instances expanded with their overrides (u1e_nested); no export needed

scene

a Unity scene as an Unreal level: export (in a window), import, readback, and the fidelity gate against its own baseline.

u2ue scene - a Unity scene as an Unreal level, and the proof it still looks like the Unity scene.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> scene export [--out DIR]
    py -m u2ue --project <name> scene import
    py -m u2ue --project <name> scene readback
    py -m u2ue --project <name> scene check [--no-parity] [--json FILE]
    py -m u2ue --project <name> scene --dry
    py -m u2ue --project <name> scene import|readback|check --dir DIR --content /Game/...   (a trial: its own folder and root)
    py -m u2ue.verbs.scene --selftest

  export    the scene as glTF (glTFast: meshes, materials and textures one to one, inactive subtrees listed, the terrain baked from
            its TerrainData). It runs in the game's own Unity Editor, so this verb never touches an editor: it prints the trigger a
            window drops (.RUN_SCENE_EXPORT, whose one line is the output folder) and refuses by name. The exporter is the reference
            port's Editor script; for any other game it is planned to ship as the package's Editor assembly.
  import    the exported glTF into a NEW Unreal level through Interchange's own scene pipeline - the engine's default glTF stack,
            nothing hand-placed (Unreal, headless, from native PowerShell, one Unreal at a time).
  readback  the saved level read back headless: every actor and attach chain, every material slot and its root material, every
            material instance's parameters, every texture asset in the scene's folder, the lights (Unreal, headless).
  check     the fidelity gate (scene_fidelity_gate.py): hierarchy, materials, textures, lighting and placement against Unity's own
            files and the scene's OWN measured baseline (<scene dir>/fidelity-baseline.json); exit 1 the moment one moves, 2 when an
            input or the baseline is missing (no editor runs).
  --dry     the scene's paths, opened, and the host's state.

The project names its scene - "scene": {"unity": "Assets/<Scene>.unity", "name": "<Name>", "dir": "<scene work folder>",
"content": "/Game/.../<Name>"} - and the tools read it as U2UE_SCENE_NAME / _DIR / _CONTENT / _UNITY.

parity

the game's rules on every runtime they run on, compared by float bits with a characterised allowance.

u2ue parity - do the game's rules give the same answers on every runtime they run on (BASICS sections 4-5).

    py -m u2ue --project <name> parity [--dir DIR] [--require ENGINE ...] [--characterise]

A port that moves the rules into an engine-free model runs the SAME model on Unity (Mono) and on the Unreal host (CoreCLR), and a
headless runner beside them. Each run writes a digest: <dir>/logic-<Engine>.txt, one `key=value` row per case after a
`digestVersion=N` line, every float as its float32 BIT PATTERN in hex (Mono prints float "R" with 9 digits, .NET prints the shortest -
identical bits spell two ways; compare bits, never text). This wraps .opus-tools/logic_diff.py (the facade never rewrites a tool):
every row compared across every engine found; a difference is RED unless the characterised allowance (<dir>/logic-allowance.json,
written by --characterise from the reports on disk) pins that exact row to its exact bits AND to one ULP - so a new row, a moved
value or a wider gap stays red. Exit 0 agree, 1 a row differs, 2 refused (a required report missing, or digest versions differ).
The project names its digest folder as parity.dir; a project whose model has not run yet has none, and is refused.

digest

the game's rule cases answered with no engine: on CoreCLR (Headless) and on that Unity's own Mono (UnityMono).

u2ue digest - a game's rule cases answered with NO engine, on both runtimes a port has to agree across (logic-port skill step 9;
BASICS section 5): CoreCLR - what the Unreal host and a headless runner use - and that Unity version's OWN Mono. Nothing opens a
window and nothing takes focus. `u2ue parity` then marks the two answer sheets against each other by the bit.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> digest run --entry Ns.Class.Method --cases A.cs [B.cs ...] [--refs X.dll ...] [--dir DIR]
    py -m u2ue --project <name> digest faithful
    py -m u2ue.verbs.digest --selftest

The entry is a static method returning the digest text (string) or a U2ue.Runtime.Digest. --refs defaults to the project's model:
every model layer built for netstandard2.1 (the build Unity loads) and U2ue.Runtime. `run` writes, into DIR (default parity.dir):
  logic-Headless.txt    the cases compiled with the .NET SDK and run on CoreCLR (net8.0)
  logic-UnityMono.txt   the same cases compiled by that Unity's csc.exe and run on its mono-bdwgc.exe (the Editor's own runtime
                        build), with logic-UnityMono.provenance.json naming the Mono and whether it is MEASURED faithful
WHY UNITY'S MONO CAN STAND IN FOR THE EDITOR, AND ONLY WHERE MEASURED: a float rule's answer depends on the runtime that JITs it, and
Mono is the odd one out (it keeps float intermediates wider, so `a * b + c` can land one ULP from CoreCLR's). MEASURED 2026-10-16 on
Unity 6000.3.16f1: the reference game's digest (383 rows) computed this way equals the digest the Unity Editor wrote, row for row,
including the 35 rows where Mono and CoreCLR differ; and its CoreCLR run here equals the recorded headless digest.
  `faithful`  re-measures that: the project's "mono.faithful" block names the Editor that recorded a digest, the cases and DLLs it
              ran, and that digest. Exit 0 = identical; the measurement is written as a conformance bake
              (shared/conformance/mono-standalone-facts-<major.minor>.json, with unity.version) - the next `run` on that Unity reads it.
A Unity version with no such bake is labelled UNMEASURED in the provenance: Mono's answer, not yet proven to be the Editor's.

host

the game's OWN Unreal project, made as a customer makes one: create, install, compile, generate, wire, publish, run.

u2ue host - the game's OWN Unreal project, made by the toolkit step by step as a customer makes one (u2ue/hostproject.py:
HostProject; the u2ue-logic skill's step 10).

    py -m u2ue --project <name> host plan              every step: the command it runs and the line that proves it
    py -m u2ue --project <name> host status            each step's record (host-<step>.json): proven, failed, or not run
    py -m u2ue --project <name> host <step> [--dry]    run ONE step: create, install, compile, generate, wire, publish, run
    py -m u2ue.verbs.host --selftest

The Unreal steps (compile, generate, publish, run) REFUSE while the project's adapter says the Unreal host is busy, and when this
shell's PATH would hide .NET from UnrealSharp (run them from native PowerShell); each is judged by its proof line in its own log
(and `run` also by the digest file being written after the run started). Exit 0 = the step proved itself; 1 = it ran and did not;
2 = refused before it ran.

ui

a Unity UI screen converted to a folder Unreal reads; the generic uGUI / TextMeshPro library's tests.

u2ue ui - a Unity UI screen, captured, converted to a folder Unreal reads, and rebuilt by Unity's own layout rules.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> ui convert <capture dir> --screen NAME [--out DIR]
    py -m u2ue --project <name> ui test
    py -m u2ue --project <name> ui capture
    py -m u2ue.verbs.ui --selftest

  convert   one capture -> one screen folder: the capture itself, its sprites, and each TextMeshPro font's TTF located by the GUID
            the font asset recorded and PROVEN by identical glyph indices (a font that fails is refused). The project's Unity
            Assets are searched (unity.assets). DIR defaults to <work.ui>/screens/NAME when the project names work.ui. A DIR that
            exists must hold a screen.json: the converter replaces the folder it writes, so a folder it did not write is refused.
  test      the generic UI library's own tests (u2ue/runtime/U2ue.Ui.Tests, headless): uGUI's layout, meshes, raycast and
            TextMeshPro's layout held to Unity's captures, with no game reference.
  capture   runs in the project's own Unity Editor, in Play mode (it reads uGUI's resolved state and TextMeshPro's per-glyph
            layout). The reference capture is an Editor script behind a local HTTP bridge; for any other game it is planned to ship as
            the package's Editor assembly, which waits on installing the package into a project (the owner's decision) - refused
            here, by name.

The library is the converter's generic part (u2ue/runtime/U2ue.Ui); a game's panel bindings stay the game's. Nothing here
launches Unity or Unreal.

window

ONE Unity measurement window from a data file: idle-gated, owner-stoppable, nothing replaced, md5-held.

u2ue window - ONE Unity measurement window, from a data file (pillars 4, 10, 11). It replaces hand-cloned window scripts,
each made by search-and-replace on the one before (which broke once, on half-renamed frames).

    py -m u2ue --project <name> window check <spec.json>     every refusal judged now, nothing touched (exit 0 = it would start)
    py -m u2ue --project <name> window run <spec.json>       wait for the owner to be away, then run it
    py -m u2ue.verbs.window --selftest                       the whole flow against a SIMULATED editor - no Unity is touched

A SPEC (JSON) - what the window measures, never how it is kept safe:
    {"label": "g23", "why": "...", "probes": ["EffectPhotoProbe"],
     "inputs": [{"from": "<lane>/x6/effect-photo-list-x6.tsv", "to": "effect-photo-list-x6.tsv"}],      copied INTO the conformance dir
     "trigger": {"file": ".RUN_EFFECT_PHOTO", "lines": ["list:effect-photo-list-x6.tsv", "record:effect-photo-unity-x6.json"]},
     "outputs": ["effect-photo-unity-x6.json"], "wait_seconds": 900}
THE SAFETY, written once, here, for every window (the owner's editor is the owner's):
  - starts only after 600 s with no cursor move and no key or button (lane/wait_quiet.ps1 - its own QUIET line, nothing else), and a
    presence watch (lane/wait_presence.ps1) stops it at its next step when the owner returns: the probes are removed, nothing else runs
  - refuses: Play mode or no bridge, the editor lock held, an output that already exists (nothing is replaced), the trigger already
    down, a DIFFERENT file already where an input goes, a probe already in the Editor folder, a probe that does not compile HEADLESS
  - holds the editor lock (.opus-tools/.locks/unity-editor.lock) for its whole life; md5s every conformance record (but its outputs)
    and the project's guard files before and after - a change is a FAIL; console_check reset before, judged after
  - deletes the probes only while the editor is idle (twice, 5 s apart: an earlier window deleted them mid-import) and waits until the editor DLL no
    longer holds their names
  - never answers a modal, never enters Play, never runs the Test Runner
The project names: unity.root, unity.probe_dir (the Editor folder probes are dropped into), unity.guard (files whose md5 must hold).

trial

a route's TRIAL in Unreal from a data file: build, resave, read, judge, photos; one Unreal at a time, stoppable.

u2ue trial - a route's TRIAL in Unreal, from a data file (pillars 4, 10, 11). It replaces hand-copied queue scripts
(lane/queue_*.ps1, one near-identical block per trial): the trial is data, and the runner is written once.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> trial plan <spec.json> [...]     every command and variable each step would run - nothing runs
    py -m u2ue --project <name> trial run <spec.json> [...]      run them in order; one Unreal at a time; stoppable between steps
    py -m u2ue --project <name> trial stop                       ask the running trials to stop at their next step boundary
    py -m u2ue.verbs.trial --selftest                            the runner against a SIMULATED executor - nothing launches

A SPEC (JSON) - what the trial tries, never how it is run:
    {"label": "rc1", "why": "...", "dir": "{lane}/ratecurve/rc1", "root": "/Game/<Game>/Trials/RC1",
     "requires": {"file": "{vfxport}/build_niagara.py", "contains": "# WARMBURST \(10-16"},       optional: unmet = SKIPPED, said
     "keys": {"file": "{dir}/keys.txt"} | {"list": ["prefab.<guid>", ...]} | {"script": ["{lane}/x/keys.py", "{dir}/keys.txt"]},
     "switches": {"VFXPORT_RATECURVE": "1"},                                    set for the BUILD only, removed after it
     "steps": [{"build": {"batch": 6, "max_seconds": 9000}}, {"resave": {"max_seconds": 3600}},
               {"read": {"frames": 90, "max_seconds": 3600, "out": "rb_rc1.json"}},
               {"judge": {"argv": ["{lane}/ratecurve/ratecurve_check.py", "{dir}/rb_rc1.json"]}},
               {"photos": {"times": [0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0], "max_seconds": 3600}},
               {"py": {"argv": ["{lane}/meshvcol/trial_sheets.py", "{label}", "{photos}", "{root_dir}", "--all"], "unreal": false}}]}
  placeholders: {dir} {root} {label} {lane} {effects} {tools} {vfxport} {photos} (= <effects>/photos/<label>) {root_dir} (the
  content root on disk: <uproject dir>/Content/<root after /Game/>)
THE STEPS, each the same commands and variables a hand-written queue ran:
  build    fx17_build.ps1 -KeysFile <dir>/keys.txt -Tag <label> -Batch N -MaxSeconds S, with the switches, U2UE_CONTENT_ROOT=root,
           U1E_BUILD_NEWEST / U1E_BUILD_REFUSED in <dir>; its u1e-build-only.json copied to <dir>/build-only-<label>.json - no record,
           or nothing BUILT, ends the trial; a key asked for that the record does not hold (the build's own -MaxSeconds stopped it)
           is NAMED in <dir>/unbuilt-<label>.txt - a delta trial's keys file - and the trial is PARTIAL, its built keys still read
           and photographed. Size S from the measured rate: about 45 min per batch of 6 heavy (mesh) keys on the reference host
  resave   u1e_py.ps1 -Script u1e_resave.py with U1E_RESAVE_PKG=root
  built    no build: the systems already under the root, one per key (a read of an existing build - u2ue conform)
  read     u1e_py.ps1 -Script u1e_color_size_readback.py with U1E_RB_SYSTEMS = the BUILT systems, U1E_RB_FRAMES (and U1E_RB_DT
           when "dt" is given); copied to <dir>/<out>
  judge    py <argv> [with "env"] - its exit and last lines are the trial's verdict (a red judge is FAIL; the photos are still taken, to LOOK at);
           "plant": {"argv": [...]} runs the same judge on a record it MUST refuse - a plant that passes FAILS the step
  photos   u1e_py.ps1 -Script u1e_fx_photo.py with U1E_PHOTO_SYSTEMS, U1E_PHOTO_TIMES, U2UE_PHOTOS_DIR=<photos> - judged by its
           Capture (u2ue/capture.py), never its exit: a system or frame missing PARTIAL and named, no result FAIL
  unreal   any other Unreal script: u1e_py.ps1 -Script <script> with its "env"; its "out" (in the effects dir) copied to <dir>, none
           written FAILS (a probe that builds in memory, e.g. u1e_trail_real_probe for what a built system trims)
  py       any other tool (a reader that runs Unreal itself: "unreal": true waits for no Unreal first and names the runner as host)
THE RULES, once: runs alone (no lane queue, no other trial); waits for no Unreal before every Unreal step; the inherited VFXPORT_ /
U1E_ / U2UE_ variables are dropped and the project's loaded (Project.env); refuses a PATH whose dotnet marker lacks the trailing
backslash UnrealSharp needs (the Bash chain: launch from native PowerShell); a STOP file is read between steps and between trials -
a stop never kills a step mid-way (only the runner can stop cleanly).
The trials run from a SNAPSHOT of the code parts (u2ue/run.py Run): `run` copies them, then runs the trials in
a child process whose U2UE_PART_* point at the copies - an edit to the live converter mid-queue cannot change what runs. The record
<dir>/trial-<label>.json names every step's verdict, the copy it ran ("run") and the commit of each toolkit tree it was taken at.

conform

data-first conformance over all keys: Unity's particle state (one generic probe) against Niagara's readback, paired by file id.

u2ue conform - DATA-FIRST conformance over all keys at once: Unity's own particle state, read per system by the
generic probe, against what the built Niagara systems compute, read back - paired by the prefab's system file id, judged on numbers.
Why: on the reference port, ONE class-wide readback found a rule (every non-prewarmed burst born one warm-up tick late) that nights of
per-effect photos had missed; this makes that readback a standing check.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> conform cases --name <run> [--keys FILE] [--times 0.1,0.3,0.6,1.0]
        writes, from the project's IR: <conformance>/<run>-cases.json (one ParticleCaseProbe case per key: its prefab placed by the
        game's effect spawn, seed pinned, read from a restart at each time), lane/windows/<run>.json (the Unity window that runs it)
        and lane/trials/<run>-read.json (the Unreal read of the same keys' BUILT systems at the probe's step, 0.02 s)
    py -m u2ue --project <name> conform diff --unity <particle-cases record> --unreal <readback record> [--report FILE]
        per key, per active emitter: the live COUNT at every probe time and the FIRST BIRTH (time minus the oldest age, both sides),
        Unity's system found by its file id, Unreal's emitter by the converter's own naming (niagara_names.system_names)
        --report writes the rows (each with the emitter's file id and the numbers judged) STAMPED with the judge's id and inputs
    py -m u2ue --project <name> conform latest [--run NAME] [--dir DIR]
        the newest stamped report under <lane>/conform of ONE run (its Unity record NAME-unity.json; the project's
        conform.standing_run unless --run): "CONFORM OK n of m (x %)" - STALE (exit 1) when another judge made it
    py -m u2ue --project <name> conform classes --report FILE [--build u1e-build-newest.json]
        every LATE / EARLY row NAMED by the converter's own note on that emitter or a measured signature (NAMED_MISSES), only
        when direction and size agree - the rest UNNAMED, listed: the work
    py -m u2ue.verbs.conform --selftest      identical records agree; a planted 0.03 s late birth FAILS; a count off FAILS; an
                                             emitter missing on one side is named, never dropped
VERDICTS per emitter, both sides read at Unity's sample times only (like with like): OK (a "sub-frame" note when the births
differ inside one frame) | LATE / EARLY (first DRAWN on a different frame) | COUNT (more than max(1, 5 %) apart at a time, or only
one side drew anything at the times read) | BIRTH UNREAD (the counts agree and no first birth can be read: an infinite lifetime, a capped list) |
UNPAIRED (one side has no such emitter - named with the side) | NO DATA (neither side
drew a particle at the times read: an emitter alive only between samples is not judged, and is counted as such).

judge

every judge the trials run, the trials that run it, and whether its plant can refuse (its --selftest, or a trial's declared plant).

u2ue judge - every judge the project's trials run, the trials that run it, and whether its plant can refuse (u2ue/judge.py: Judge).

    py -m u2ue --project <name> judge             each judge: selftest / declared (a trial's plant) / NO PLANT
    py -m u2ue --project <name> judge --prove     runs each judge's --selftest; exit 1 when one fails or a judge has no plant
    py -m u2ue.verbs.judge --selftest             the Judge class's own selftest
A judge with no plant has only ever passed, which is indistinguishable from a judge that was switched off (pillar 5).

extract

Unity prefabs -> the engine-neutral IR (no editor runs).

u2ue extract - a Unity project's effects -> the engine-neutral IR.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> extract [--steps index,keys,ir] [--out DIR] [--resolve FILE]

Steps, in order, each one's output the next one's input:
  index   the guid index (t1_guid_index.py)                                     -> work.guid_index
          + when the project names its Editor (unity.editor): the built-in shader names (u1e_builtin_names.py)
                                                                               -> work.effects/builtin_extra_names.json
  keys    the project's effect keys, from its ADAPTER (u2ue/adapters)            -> work.resolve
            unity_project     every prefab that holds a ParticleSystem (u2ue/keys.py), Unity's spawn rule
            <game>            a game adapter (u2ue/adapters/<game>.py): the keys the game's own code fires, its pool's spawn rule
          then checked: every key agrees with the adapter's spawn rule (u1e_ir picks the rule by the key's prefix)
  ir      one IR file per READ key (u1e_ir.py)                                  -> work.effects/ir + u1e-ir.json

  --out DIR       the IR and its summary go under DIR instead of work.effects: a staging run that leaves the project's IR alone
  --resolve FILE  the keys are read from FILE instead of work.resolve (a sample); the keys step cannot run with it

The run is defined by the project file and these flags only: U1E_* and VFXPORT_* variables inherited from the calling shell are
REMOVED (and named) before any tool starts - a switch left over from another run must not change an extraction.

Checked after the ir step, exit 1 on any:
  every READ key of the resolve is in the summary, as an IR file or a NAMED refusal - none dropped
  every IR file is on disk and parses, with its emitter count
  every "Assets/..." path an IR names exists in THIS project's tree (a path from another project's index cannot pass)

check

the toolkit's selftests, the project's field gates, the measured rules' Unity versions.

u2ue check - is the bag sound, and does this project's IR meet every field gate.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> check [--only selftests|gates|facts|model] [--tool NAME ...]

  selftests  every tool's OWN offline selftest (u2ue/survey/pt1_selftests.RUNS - read off each tool by hand, none invented here),
             then the project file's own rows (`selftests`: the gates written against that one game); each must exit 0; run with
             the inherited U2UE_ / U1E_ / VFXPORT_ variables dropped (a PIN kept, tools.clean_env) and the project's own U2UE_ paths
             set, so no switch left in a shell can change what a plant meets. A selftest that is never run
             here says its measured reason (NOT_RUN, or the project's not_run). v4_write_gate's --selftest also runs its STATIC gate, which
             types only part of the converter's writes: its PLANTS must bite ("SELFTEST PASS"); its gate result is not counted - the
             authority on refused writes, v4_msg_gate over the built packages, runs per trial.
  gates      yaml_field_gate over THIS project's IR (every key of every enabled module read by shuriken_ir or excused with the values
             it may take) and ir_field_gate (every field the IR carries named by the converter or DELIBERATELY_UNREAD with its reason)

  facts      every measured Unity rule with the Unity version it was measured on, against the project's unity.version: a rule
             measured on another version is named UNVERIFIED for this project (reported, not a failure)
  model      layer_gate and host_gate on the engine-free model the project names (model.*); a project with no model is told so

Exit 1 when any one fails. Nothing launches Unreal or Unity; below normal priority.

build

IR -> Niagara systems under the project's content root (Unreal, headless).

u2ue build - the project's effect IR -> Niagara systems under its content root.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> build [--keys FILE] [--tag TAG] [--batch N] [--no-resave] [--dry]

  keys     every READ key of the project's resolve with an IR file (not refused) - or the list in FILE (comma / newline separated)
  steps    the asset-name table (fx17_asset_names.py: names two different Unity files would share, per project) -> records/
           asset_names.json; then fx17_build.ps1 -KeysFile -Tag -Batch [-Resave] - u1e_build in headless Unreal, batched compiles,
           the resave, the record kept as records/u1e-build-<TAG>.json
  --dry    print the plan (keys, paths, the guard's verdict) and run nothing

Refuses while the Unreal host is busy (the project's adapter answers: any Unreal running, or the game's own queues - verbs/_ue.py). The tools read
the project's U2UE_* environment; U1E_* / VFXPORT_* variables inherited from the shell are REMOVED and named,
so the build is the project's defaults - the build an acceptance rebuild makes.

read

the built systems read back frame by frame (Unreal, headless).

u2ue read - read back the systems a build made, frame by frame.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> read [--tag TAG] [--frames N] [--dry]

Every BUILT system of records/u1e-build-<TAG>.json is simulated headless in Unreal and its particles read per frame
(u1e_color_size_readback.py through u1e_py.ps1: position, velocity, colour, size, age ... at 1/60 s steps) into
records/rb_<TAG>_<N>.json - the input every read-back check of the bag takes - with its capture summary (u2ue/readback.py): a
system that captured no frame, or fewer than asked, is named and the verb exits 1. Refuses while the Unreal host is busy.

photo

the built systems photographed, paired with Unity's frames (Unreal, headless).

u2ue photo - photograph the systems a build made and compose the Unity / Unreal pair sheets.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> photo [--tag TAG] [--times 0.1,0.3,0.6,1.0] [--dry]

Every BUILT system of records/u1e-build-<TAG>.json is drawn headless at each time (u1e_fx_photo.py through u1e_py.ps1, the
project's photos/unreal), then u1e_photo_sheet.py pairs each with Unity's frames where the project has them (photos/unity_hdr,
taken by EffectPhotoProbe in that project's own Editor - a Unity run, the project owner's call) into photos/sheets. A sheet is
evidence only once LOOKED AT. Refuses while the Unreal host is busy.

The run is judged by its CAPTURE (u2ue/capture.py), never by the tool's exit: the result record is kept beside the frames, and a
system with no judgeable frame (an error, no background, no frame) or a frame asked for and not written by THIS run is named; a system never
captured fails the verb.

report

the acceptance page from the project's records.

u2ue report - the acceptance report for a project, built from ITS records.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> report [--out FILE]

Runs report_build.py - the acceptance page's own builder - with the project's U2UE_* environment: the IR summary,
the build records, the sweep and the photo sheets are read from work.effects / work.records, and the page names the project. The
default page is <work.effects>/report/<name>_acceptance.html. A decision's evidence picture shows only when the report holds the
key it pictures. Nothing launches Unreal or Unity; below-normal priority.

The report reads what is THERE: a key never built reads "never built", a sweep or a photo screen not run reads absent - so a
project's first report, before any build, already names every key it will have to account for.

The run is defined by the project file and these flags only: U1E_* and VFXPORT_* variables inherited from the calling shell are
REMOVED (and named) first, as extract does.

metrics

the port's numbers, each from a record, with its definition.

u2ue metrics - the port's numbers for a project, every one COMPUTED FROM ITS RECORDS with its denominator and its definition.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> metrics [--json FILE]

Nothing here is estimated, sampled or remembered: a number this verb cannot compute from a record on disk is printed ABSENT with
the record it needs, and a tool that stops stops this verb. Each input's age is printed, and an input OLDER than the newest build is
marked STALE (it describes builds that are gone) - a stale number is never presented as current.

The emitter numbers are the ACCEPTANCE PAGE's (lane/report_build.py, run here with the project's environment), never recounted
here. The page picks each key's record (an acceptance override, else the acceptance rebuild's chunk, else the newest build, else a
trial), counts a log as drawn only when it carries modules, and applies the measured never-fires rule over whole sub-emitter chains
(fx17/unity_never_fires.json). A recount of the newest records that skipped those rules (skipped logs counted as drawn, the chain
rule missed) was measured wrong both ways, which is why this verb never recounts.

THE DEFINITIONS (they are the claim; a number quoted without its definition is not one):
  keys        the project's effect keys (its IR summary), each with the verdict of the record the page chose for it
  drawn       an emitter whose log carries modules - it draws in Unreal
  absent      an emitter the build named EMITTER-ABSENT, split by the page:
                as Unity - absent exactly as in Unity, each by a MEASURED or READ rule in the converter's own words (the game
                           never starts it; Unity never fires it - measured; Unity draws / emits nothing there itself; a missing
                           material Unity has no particle to draw on) - no gap
                gap      - every other: Unity draws it, Unreal does not - a NAMED gap; charged to its ROOT (an absent parent's
                           children to the ancestor absent for its own reason), so a root's count is what porting it brings back
  coverage    drawn / (drawn + gap) - of the emitters Unity draws, the share Unreal draws
  measured    drawn emitters with no "SUBSTITUTED" note - drawn by a rule measured against Unity, not a named stand-in
  data        the readback sweep (checks_summary.json): per check, emitters checked and FAILs, summed over every part
  image       the photo screen (u1e_sheet_screen over the sheets listing): pairs compared, pairs flagged for a big difference,
              and of the flagged how many carry a ONE DRAW (RANDDRAW) or GRIDTICK label - frames where a difference is the
              capture, not the port
  machine     the chosen records' own per-key seconds (delete .. finalize), summed and per key
  routes      the converter's verified switches (patch_flip_defaults' TABLE, DISTINCT switch names - one switch read in two files
              has two rows) flipped default ON with their evidence, and the switches named deliberately OFF (flip_audit's
              DELIBERATE_OFF, each with what it waits on)
Agent tempo (how long a route took the agent from FOUND to FLIPPED) is not in these records - it is the git history's, and is
reported by `u2ue tempo` when that exists, never folded in here.

tempo

each verified route's first code -> verified flip, read off git.

u2ue tempo - how fast the toolkit's verified routes went from first code to verified flip, read off git.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> tempo [--json FILE] [--since YYYY-MM-DD]

THE DEFINITION (it is the claim):
  a route    one switch of patch_flip_defaults' TABLE (distinct names; a switch read in two files has two rows) - each one was
             written default OFF, proven, trialed and flipped default ON with its evidence row
  first code the earliest commit, over every file the switch's rows name, whose ADDED lines carry the switch name
  flipped    per file, the earliest commit whose added lines carry its default-ON read (environ.get("NAME", "1")); the route
             is flipped when its LAST file is - and only if EVERY file reads it default ON today (a TABLE row is evidence a switch
             may flip, not proof that it did: a switch held OFF can have a row and still read "0")
  tempo      flipped - first code, in hours of wall clock (commit author times). A route whose first code already reads it
             default ON (no OFF stage on record) is counted apart, never as tempo 0.
What this does NOT measure, said so it is never implied: the time from FOUND (the defect first seen) to first code, the
agent's tokens, and the machine's build hours (`u2ue metrics`). A file whose history holds no default-ON line names the route
ABSENT here, with the file - never a guessed date.

cycle

every pillar of the product checked: PASS / FAIL / HELD by a named decision / ABSENT (no check yet).

u2ue cycle - every pillar of the product checked, the way it is checked every work cycle.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> cycle [--pillar N ...] [--dry]
    py -m u2ue.verbs.cycle --selftest

Each pillar (u2ue/pillars.py) runs its checks; the record goes to <records>/cycle-<stamp>.json and cycle-latest.json, and the NEXT
cycle reads it for every Trend (a number that must not move the wrong way). Exit 1 when any pillar is FAIL - red stops the cycle.
An ABSENT pillar is not a pass: it names the work that would give it a check.

tool

one tool of the toolkit run by hand, found by its file name, with the project's variables (u2ue/env.py).

u2ue tool - one tool of the toolkit, run by hand with the project's U2UE_* variables. A tool reads its paths only from
those variables (u2ue/env.py) and refuses without them, so this is how a tool is run outside a verb.

    py -m u2ue --project <name> tool <tool.py | tool.ps1> [args ...]
    py -m u2ue --project <name> tool --selftest

The tool is found by its FILE NAME in the toolkit's parts (u2ue/tools.py PARTS); a name in none of them, or in more than one, is
refused with what was found. A .py runs on this Python, a .ps1 on PowerShell 7 - both below normal priority, in the tool's own
folder, their output streamed through and their exit code returned. A tool that starts Unreal keeps its own guards (one Unreal at a
time); `tool` adds none and removes none.

release

the package as a repo: assembled from the toolkit's own trees by one manifest, secrets refused, public readiness counted.

u2ue release - the package as a repo, assembled from the toolkit's own trees by one manifest (u2ue/release.py: Release).

    py -m u2ue release --to <DIR> [--dry]     assemble the repo into DIR (empty, or a release checkout): what ships, what is left
                                              out and why, the public-readiness count; --dry writes nothing
    py -m u2ue release --check --to <DIR>     exit 1 when DIR differs from what the manifest would write (a stale release)
    py -m u2ue.verbs.release --selftest       a planted secret refuses; a run record, an image and an oversized file are named out;
                                              a planted game name is counted; a second assembly writes nothing; drift is caught

Exit 0 = assembled (or current); 1 = --check found a difference; 2 = refused (a secret, a folder that is not a release, no --to).
Nothing is committed or pushed: the repo's history and its remote are the owner's.

21. Reference

Who this is for: the toolkit developer and the reviewer - the file formats, environment variables, converter switches, tools and selftests, in one place to look them up. Read it when a field, a variable or a switch is named elsewhere and you need its meaning.

The tables marked generated are written by u2ue/manual/build.py from the code, so they change when the code does. Edit the code, not the table.

File formats

The project file - u2ue/projects/<name>.json

field type meaning
name string the project's name; also names the default report page
adapter string unity_project, or a game adapter's name (Chapter 18)
unity.root path the Unity project's root
unity.assets path its Assets folder
unity.version string its Unity version, e.g. 6000.3.16f1; measured rules are checked against it
unity.editor path, optional that version's Editor install, for built-in shader and material names
unity.probe_dir, unity.guard path, paths the Editor folder under the Unity root a probe is dropped into for one window, and the files whose md5 must hold across it (Chapter 8)
effects.key_source object {"kind": "particle_prefabs", "roots": [...]}; the only other kind the loader accepts is the reference port's own resolver
unreal.uproject path the Unreal host project
unreal.engine path the engine install
unreal.content_root string where built systems go, e.g. /Game/U2UE/<Name>
unreal.host object, optional the game's own Unreal project made by u2ue host: template, plugins, toolkit_plugins, sdks_root, digest (Chapter 13)
work.* paths effects, ir, guid_index, resolve, records, photos, inventory, and optionally materials (the material-parent tools' reads and outputs): where each step writes
code.roots paths the game's own C# folders, relative to the Unity root
model.root path the folder holding the engine-free model's projects
model.layers object {project: [projects it may reference]}, inner layer first
model.scan, model.hosting paths where platform members may not be declared, and the one folder where they may
model.hosts object, optional {engine: [folders holding that engine's host code]}, which the seam report reads (Chapter 5)
model.unreal_links bool, optional whether the layer gate also checks the Unreal host's links
parity.dir, parity.engines path, list where each runtime writes logic-<Engine>.txt, and which runtimes to compare
mono.faithful object, optional what digest faithful re-runs on Unity's own Mono: editor, entry, cases, refs, reference (Chapter 5)
scene object, optional the scene u2ue scene ports: unity, name, dir, content (Chapter 6)
conform.standing_run string, optional the conformance run conform latest reads unless --run names another, and the one the cycle trends (Chapter 9)
estimate_basis object, optional the port's own transcripts and runs, which token_basis.py reads to measure the token rates u2ue estimate multiplies by (the cost page)
selftests object, optional the game's own gates, runs and not_run (the selftest list below)
public_names object, optional names: the game's own names; the manual's build refuses a page holding one, and u2ue release counts the shipped files that do

The IR - one JSON file per effect key

Written by extract (u1e_ir.py over shuriken_ir.py), engine-neutral: nothing in it names an Unreal type. The reader writes to <work.effects>/ir while the gates and the build read work.ir, so work.ir must name that folder; a project file whose work.ir names another is refused when it loads.

field meaning
key, source the effect key and the prefab it was read from
rootRotation, rootScale the effect root's transform
emitters[] one entry per ParticleSystem: name; the main module (duration, looping, prewarm, startDelay, simulationSpace, scalingMode, playOnAwake, maxParticles, startLifetime, startSpeed, startColor, startSize and its axes, startRotation, gravityModifier, ringBufferMode, ...); modules (every other enabled module), emission, shape and renderer; the emitter's place in the transform chain (prefabPos, prefabRot, localScale, localRot, nodeMatrix, lossyScale, ownerScale, chainSheared); and the reader's own bookkeeping, prefixed _ (_active, _psFileID, _depth)
materials every material the emitters use, its shader and values (a variant's through its parent)
emitterCount how many emitters the effect holds
naturalLengthSeconds, naturalLengthWhy, peakSeconds how long the effect runs and when it peaks, with the reason
lifetimeSeconds the lifetime the game's code gives one spawn, or null; the reason is lifetimeWhy in the summary u1e-ir.json. Always null for a unity. key, whose game code is not read

A value Unity stores as a curve or a random range is an object, never a flattened number: {"mode": "constant", "scalar": 5, "value": 5, "readAs": "scalar (minMaxState 0)"}, where readAs says how the reader read it. yaml_field_gate and ir_field_gate (Chapter 9) hold the IR to the Unity fields on one side and the converter on the other.

The build record - records/u1e-build-<TAG>.json

Top level: package, keys, materials, meshes, textures, errors, vm1Errors (the material-parent author's), parents and the caches. Per key: key, prefab, ir, asset, shaders, seconds, emitters, saved, absentEmitters (each with its reason), converterErrors, converterWarnings, paramMisses and the verdict. The report and the metrics read only these records.

A measured fact file - shared/conformance/*.json

Written by a probe (Chapter 8): format (which ties the file to its probe, Chapter 18), unity (the version that ran it), the case's own parameters, and the raw values it observed under names the probe chooses (samples, shots, cases, ...). An error field when the probe could not finish. Never edited by hand and never replaced by a later bake: a new bake is a new file.

A parity digest - <parity.dir>/logic-<Engine>.txt

A digestVersion=N line, then one key=value row per case. Every float is written as its 8-hex-digit bit pattern. The allowance file (logic-allowance.json beside them) pins a characterised difference to its exact row and bits.

Environment variables

variable meaning
U2UE_TOOLKIT_ROOT resolve every toolkit part to <root>/<part> (the release layout)
U2UE_HOME exported to every tool: the folder that holds the u2ue package, which a tool adds to its import path to read the project through u2ue/env.py
U2UE_PART_<NAME> exported to every tool: each toolkit part's folder, as part() answers it. Set by hand, it points that one part at a copy (a pinned run)
U2UE_* (others) set by the facade from the project file for each tool it runs (U2UE_UNITY_ROOT, U2UE_IR_DIR, U2UE_EFFECTS_DIR, ...)
VFXPORT_<NAME>, U1E_<NAME> the converter's and the reader's route switches (below). The facade removes, and names, any set in the calling shell, so a run is defined by the project file and its flags only

Converter switches (generated)

Each switch is one converter route (Chapter 7). "Default today" is what the converter reads when the variable is unset. A trial's switches block (u2ue trial, Chapter 20) can still set one to 0 for an A/B. Each switch was flipped on only with an evidence row: the trial, the Unity measurement and the check that held on the reference port. Those rows, kept in the flip table, are the converter's audit trail; py -m u2ue find <SWITCH> prints them. A switch still OFF is not verified yet, and it stays OFF until a trial proves it.

A game's own gates (the ones written against its model, its adapter or its HUD) are rows in ITS project file, under selftests: runs (each {"tool", "in": a toolkit part or "home", "sub", "argv"}) and not_run ({tool: the measured reason}). The check runs them after the rows above.

22. Architecture and the UML

Who this is for: the reviewer checking how u2ue ports, and the toolkit developer changing its structure - the layers, every generated diagram, the review's findings and the use case model behind them.

This chapter is the map. The long form is the toolkit's own u2ue/ARCHITECTURE.md: the pipeline, the principles, the converter, the design read from the code, the review with each proof, and the questions a senior engineer will ask, with their answers.

Layers

flowchart TB
  F["Facade: py -m u2ue - one verb registry"]
  F --> P["Project file - where this game's files are"]
  F --> A["Adapter - this game's own rules (3 questions)"]
  F --> K["Shared knowledge - transform, facts, routes, tools"]
  F --> T["Tools - readers, converter, Unreal steps, gates, report"]
  K --> T
  A --> T
  M["The game's engine-free model"] --> RT["Runtime library (.NET) - Unity's runtime rules"]
  • The facade is the single entry point. Every verb is one row of one registry, which the command line, the verb list, find and this manual all read.
  • The project file holds every path and choice that differs between games; the adapter holds what differs between games' rules (three questions, Chapter 18). The core knows no game: adapters are discovered by name.
  • Shared knowledge is held once: the transform conventions (u2ue.transform), the measured rules and the Unity version each was measured on (facts), the converter's switches and their evidence (routes), and where each part of the toolkit lives (tools).
  • Tools stay runnable alone and keep their own selftests. A verb runs a tool as a subprocess with the project's environment; it never re-implements one.
  • The runtime library (u2ue/runtime/U2ue.Runtime, plain .NET) is what the game's engine-free model references (Chapter 5). It and the host templates (u2ue/templates/unreal, copied into the game's own Unreal project, Chapter 13) are the parts that ship into a game.

Principles

The review's yardstick is Chapter 1's three principles, each enforced rather than recommended: read or absent, never a guess (Chapter 9 has the gates); every rule measured in Unity by a probe and a judge written before the bake (Chapter 8); every change proven before it ships, behind a switch, replayed by whole_trace.py over every emitter, trialled, then flipped (Chapter 7).

The UML in this manual

Every UML view in this manual is GENERATED (from the code, from the requirements model, or for the concept model from u2ue/CONCEPTS.md) and checked on every build, so a view that names a class, a verb or a step the toolkit does not have cannot be published. The layer sketch above is drawn by hand, as are the few flowcharts in Parts I and II: sketches, not generated views. Read the generated views in this order:

  1. The concept model (below): the ideas a person needs to follow a port, each one class. It was drawn before the code, and a gate checks that every concept it calls a class exists at its own line.
  2. The use case model (Chapter 17): who uses the toolkit for what - the use case diagram, the epic's activity flow, every case fully dressed with the document each step was read from.
  3. The facade's requirements (Chapter 19): every verb as a requirement, read from its own source - its inputs, its refusals with their lines, its exits, the selftest that verifies it and the use-case steps that run it.
  4. The class model (below): the toolkit's modules and classes and how they use one another, from the code's imports and bases.
  5. The facade map (below): which modules and tool parts each verb reaches.
  6. The traceability (Appendix E): each stakeholder requirement down to the selftest that proves it.

A reviewer starts at the epic (Chapter 17), follows a step into the verb that proves it (Chapter 19), and only then opens code.

The facade's layers, read from the code

To see the class model as a diagram, run py u2ue/survey/design_diagram.py OUT.mmd --members 0 (members come from uml.py's extraction, edges from the code's own imports and class bases). --members 0 lists no members; without it each class lists its first 12 with their real signatures and counts the rest. In that diagram a dashed arrow is "imports", "runs" marks a row of the verb registry, and a hollow triangle is a base class. Read top to bottom, the facade has five layers:

  • cli (u2ue/__main__.py) - the only entry. It reads --project and asks the registry; it knows no verb by name but info, the default.
  • verbs (u2ue/verbs/__init__.py, VERBS) - one row per verb: its name, whether it needs a project and what it does; its module is u2ue/verbs/<name>.py. Dispatch, the usage text of py -m u2ue and the verb source of find all read this one table.
  • the verb modules - each a run(p, argv). No verb imports another verb: an edge inside verbs goes to _ue, the private helper the verbs that launch Unreal share (build, read, photo, host, scene), and what two verbs share lives one layer down: check and scaffold both judge a model by gates.model_failures. That move removed the last exception, verbs_scaffold using verbs_check.
  • the shared services - among them Project (one game's paths), tools (part(): every toolkit directory named once), adapters (the ports), catalog (what find searches), routes (the flip table), facts (which Unity measured each rule), keys.
  • the tools - the converter, the readers, the judges. The verbs RUN them as processes, so each still runs by hand with its own selftest; the facade loads a tool's file only to read a table it holds (routes: the flip table and the deliberately-OFF list; check: the selftest list), and u2ue.transform's selftest loads the converter to cross-check its arithmetic.
